findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate audit-log datetimes
findings.body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses this paginator with order_by="-datetime", but get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil to the field value. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so any nonempty optimized response raises TypeError while building its cursors. value_from_cursor also lacks the timestamp-to-datetime conversion required for subsequent queries. Use DateTimePaginator's key and cursor conversions for this endpoint.

findings.title: Django querysets reject the advertised negative offsets
findings.body: When advanced features are enabled, a cursor with a negative offset is passed directly to QuerySet slicing. Django does not support negative queryset indexes and raises ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported."). Consequently, the newly advertised negative-offset pagination fails instead of returning a page. Reject such cursors with BadPaginationError or implement reverse traversal using supported query operations.

findings.title: Changing Redis key types in place breaks existing buffered data
findings.body: The previous implementation stores Redis sets at the same span-buf:s:* keys that this implementation now accesses with ZADD, ZSCAN, and sorted-set Lua commands. Existing buffered segments therefore cause WRONGTYPE errors after deployment, and old workers likewise cannot access segments written by new workers during a rolling deployment. This can block ingestion and flushing until keys expire, losing buffered spans. Introduce a versioned key namespace or an explicit compatible migration/drain strategy.

findings.title: Use a non-additive aggregation when merging timestamp scores
findings.body: ZUNIONSTORE defaults to AGGREGATE SUM. If a payload already exists in the destination and is inserted again into a source buffer—for example, when replaying a child span whose parent has a redirect—merging adds its two end timestamps together. That duplicate then receives a score roughly twice its actual timestamp and survives eviction ahead of genuinely newer spans. The old set union deduplicated without changing ordering information; use an aggregation such as MAX to preserve the timestamp score in both merge operations.

findings.title: Insertion eviction ignores the configured segment span limit
findings.body: Eviction is hard-coded to 1000 spans, while SpansBuffer still accepts and stores max_segment_spans and no longer enforces it during loading. A caller configuring a smaller limit now receives segments above that limit, and a caller configuring a larger limit silently loses spans at 1000. Pass the configured limit into the insertion script and enforce it consistently, or explicitly remove the configuration contract rather than leaving it ineffective.
